prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy selected proteins

statement.case_for: After the first round my reading of B068 is unchanged in substance and sharper in framing. The discovery is a design principle: a small molecule, either a heterobifunctional PROTAC or a monovalent glue, creates a ternary complex that nature does not make, so the target is removed instead of inhibited. The chemistry is mature in the sense that matters for a chemistry prize. Ternary-complex structures, cooperativity and degrader design rules are quantitative, and independent groups have reproduced and extended the idea for two decades, including as a probe tool far outside drug discovery. Targets that no inhibitor could engage are now routinely approached. It also has the broadest base on the table, ranked by seven of eight members at opening and named as an alternative by five others. I keep the third name as Handa because the cereblon work explains thalidomide and its analogues, the glues that reached patients first, and so anchors the second branch that makes the citation a statement about the whole principle rather than one molecular format. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point. A three-name cut leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Kim and Ito, and the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands are arguably two discoveries joined by a mechanism. No degrader is approved, so the clinical proof lags the chemistry, and I may be underweighting that because of my translational orientation. Round 1 also moved support toward B011, which has four explicit supporters, a clean two-name credit and no maturity question, whereas my position has two supporters and a split on the third name. If the committee reads the third-name dispute as unresolvable, B011 is the more votable choice, and that argument has force.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling as the clearest general method, with clean two-person credit and long independent confirmation, and sees PROTACs mainly as recruitment of existing ligase biology with bifunctional molecules.
responses.response: The adoption and attribution case for Buchwald and Hartwig is strong and I accept it. I do not accept that bifunctional recruitment is merely borrowed biology. The ligase is existing biology, but the event it is made to perform, ubiquitination of a protein it never evolved to target, is created by the molecule, and that is a new pharmacological logic rather than a better way to make a known bond. That answers the chair's question on B011 from the other side: its novelty is real, with a new mechanistic step and ligand class, but it extends a bond-forming method that the 2010 prize already framed. I would ask Somfai whether he would hold that preference if the citation had to state what C-N coupling adds beyond Heck, Negishi and Suzuki. I regard B011 as the strongest alternative, not a weak one.

responses.point: Zou pairs B011 with a nitrogenase part for Rees alone, and names B068 as the strongest alternative while doubting that the PROTAC and glue lineages fit one prize.
responses.response: I understand the wish to honour two mature achievements, but the second part in this configuration is the weakest piece. Zou's own uncertainties show that a single laureate for the structure leaves out Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe, and that the N2-binding site and catalytic cycle are still open, so the citation would rest on structure alone. Adding that part would also spend the committee's three-name limit on a split with unequal weight. On the lineage question, I think one citation can cover both if it is written at the level of the principle, small-molecule direction of the ubiquitin-proteasome system, and I would rather defend that single clean statement than a two-part prize.

responses.point: Chabes also puts B068 first but names Ciulli as the third laureate, for VHL ligands and ternary-complex structural work, giving a PROTAC-centred prize.
responses.response: This is the decision the chair asked us to settle. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs drug-like and rational, and I do not dispute that. My reasons for Handa are that cereblon is the target through which both the PROTAC field and the glue field reached the clinic, and that the discovery of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a single identifiable finding, whereas Ciulli's contribution is a sustained body of design work that is harder to credit as one step. If Chabes and I both hold B068 first, I would accept Ciulli in the third place if that is what secures a fifth supporter, since the choice should not defeat the candidate. I am moved by his point that the chemistry, not the clinic, must be the test for maturity.

responses.point: Brzezinski treats B068 as a later-year candidate because of the missing approval and credit fragmentation, and prefers long-range protein electron transfer (Gray and Winkler).
responses.response: Waiting for approval would make the prize a prize for medicine, and the chair's question rightly separates the two. The reproducibility, quantitative mechanism and design rules are in place now, and that is the Chemistry test. I do take his credit-fragmentation point seriously, but the same crowding appears in any field that is large and widely repeated. I still cannot see from his round-1 statement what B053 has enabled in other laboratories, beyond giving a convincing physical explanation, so I have not moved toward it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept one citation for PROTACs and molecular glues, and whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I would accept either to avoid losing the candidate.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay B068, and whether my translational lens makes me underweight it.
Whether B011 can answer the 2010 overlap in one sentence; if it can, it may be the more likely route to five votes.
Whether B063 is chemistry or pharmaceutics, and whether its six-way credit can be cut to three.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. My Linköping work on peptides, plasmonic biosensors and hydrogels has no link to any B068, B011 or B063 candidate. I have some research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly, which does not bear on B068. Nothing has changed since round 1.
